scope: Copied standalone Wasmtime application preview on Linux x64 in three stock engines. Not the managed CLI backend, full IO/runtime parity, cross-CPU acceptance or six-platform support.
changes: Extract the proven private runner into the shared runtime used by diagnostics and source-independent mains.
Own process-level host IO on the supervisor, retaining guest pthreads, raw bytes, asynchronous completion and main-thread cwd behavior.
Use relative native-library lookup and verified local cache/library identities; restore normal buffered output before owned-process exit.
Prepare base pages locally without changing caller resource limits; preserve required 96 MiB worker reservations.

limitations: Native compilation still uses maintainer C tools.
Native caches currently infer build-host CPU features; relocation tests do not establish portability to a different CPU.
The experimental C loader still rejects empty environments and environment blocks above one MiB; general environment acceptance remains open.
Complete WASI descriptors, dynamic imports, keepalive/cancellation and reusable disposal remain unimplemented.
This preview packages one native platform and no additional runtime Lean module data.

preservedFailures.classification: Supplementary harness used ordinary JS teardown, adding a Node closed-stdout diagnostic. The retry uses the deployed owned-process flush/_Exit sequence, retaining exact original C oracle and byte/error/status assertions.

Node rejected a parent V8 heap flag replayed as an explicit Worker flag. Both internal worker paths now use their cwd preload and existing explicit heap/stack resourceLimits; the fresh three-engine retry passes.

Supplementary native oracle setup: Lean --run cannot evaluate same-module initialize declarations. Retry loads the unchanged compiled module through an import-only Runner.lean. Original Lean application, C-compiled control, inputs and assertions unchanged. No deployed target was run before the first comparison failed.

Complete general imports/descriptors, runtime lifetime and module-data support.
Integrate automatic helper provisioning and compilation into the managed package; repair and rerun Bun suite acceptance.
Validate all six native platforms and complete language/API coverage.
